why: bin/cmd/artifactgate's Bash branch matches record paths by a ROOT-RELATIVE regex over command text (_record_re/_redirect_re), so a redirect into a scratch git worktree's copy of a charter is refused as a write to a record of truth, while the same gate's Edit/Write branch asks door.locate(), which answers None for that path. The two branches of one gate disagree about one path. Measured 2026-10-08 (scratchpad gate_probe.py, verdict() called directly): `cd /tmp/claude-1000/bare.AbCd && git show 9edee02e:cairn/machines/rehearsal/intention+why.json > cairn/machines/rehearsal/intention+why.json` -> REFUSED; door.locate('/tmp/claude-1000/bare.AbCd/cairn/machines/rehearsal/intention+why.json') -> None. Met live on 996668eceef1's bare predict; it makes voyage_craft.md clause 4.4 (`git show A:<path> > <path>`) unrunnable as typed whenever a charter is in writes_to; the way through was `git checkout A -- <dir>`. The docstring records co-occurrence as a deliberate trade, but this is not co-occurrence — the record path IS the redirect target; it is the path being the wrong root.
